change_summary: SPE-4794: make brief -> act -> memory_write -> events_emit -> handoff_to_hermes the default production turn for every desk seat without waiting on Phase 0.5 code. G-1 passes for bot-00-programming-lead on every path this branch touches. The new skill resolves to bot-00 through the existing skills/desk-bootstrap/** rule, and the other twelve paths are LEAD's docs, grokbot/** and scripts/generate-templates.py. No path is unowned and none is foreign.

The seven committed grokbot templates are exactly what scripts/generate-templates.py produces from the new BASE_SKILLS, so the seat-default change is reproducible rather than hand-applied.
The gate self-test suite passes unchanged: 157 tests. The gates themselves were not weakened to accommodate this change.

The skill documents brief -> act -> memory_write -> events_emit -> handoff_to_hermes in that order; memory_brief plus its etag is stated as the precondition for repo work and brief_etag as the receipt field; degraded mode is defined and requires a recorded human ack that the seat never types itself; user-ragflow and user-hindsight are named as forbidden seat paths in both the skill and grokbot/README.md; the skills list/invoke-until-skills.approve rule appears in the skill, the operating model and the pack README; the five reserved packet_* fields and SPE-4792 appear in both the skill and docs/vps-agent-bus.md.

G-2 fails closed on this receipt while approved_by is empty. That empty field is intentional — LEAD does not self-approve, and the PR stays draft until QUALITY stamps it. It is not a completed approval and not a passing gate.

Greptile P1 4141824942 was a real defect and is fixed. desk_brief returns no etag on success, so the original trigger 'the response carried no etag' would have made every gateway-backed turn degraded and a human ack the price of ordinary work. Degraded mode is now defined as the brief FAILING (empty with a reason, deadline-cut, tool unlisted, or an etag-bearing tool returning none), a successful brief from a tool with no etag field is explicitly not degraded, and the recorded marker for desk_brief is generated_at, named in the receipt field.

Greptile P1 4141824950 was a real defect and is fixed. A degraded turn that got its ack and finished the work now emits implementation.completed with payload.degraded and the ack id; ticket.blocked is reserved for the turn that stopped without an ack. docs/handoff-contracts.md routes on kind, so the original wording would have sent LEAD chasing a blocker for work that was ready for review.

Greptile P2 4141824957 was a real gap and is documented where LEAD owns the surface. The doctor's _declared_skills() derives from prompts/<bot_id>.xml plus a hard-coded three-name tuple, so BASE_SKILLS in the generator does not reach it and a green skills row is silent about desk-production-loop. The one-line SYSTEMS fix is named in scripts/generate-templates.py, in the skill §4, and in this receipt's blockers. LEAD did not edit bot-01's code or another seat's prompt to close it.
The Greptile round did not weaken or widen anything: the templates still regenerate identically, G-7 still passes, the 157 gate tests still pass, and G-1/G-3 still pass on the same fourteen paths.
G-1 and G-3 still pass for bot-00-programming-lead across all fourteen paths after the Greptile fixes. No new path entered the diff.

Greptile P1 4141919305 was a real and serious defect, and is fixed. A failed desk_brief is a fully populated response with the failure nested under substrate.error (or recall.error) and NO top-level reason, so the previous success test would have read a substrate outage as a quiet ticket and let a seat edit without the ack. New §2.1 makes the verdict substrate.error absent AND recall.error absent AND tool listed AND not deadline-cut, states in bold that a populated response is not a successful brief, and says there is no top-level reason to look for. The L1 tree, §3, the never-table, the failure modes, the gate mapping, a rewritten bad example and docs/desk-operating-model.md point 1 all carry it.

Greptile P1 4141919330 was a real defect and is fixed. generated_at is the wall clock at assembly, and a cache hit returns the original value for the cache window, so it cannot identify a revision or support comparison. It is now recorded as brief_read_at with cached alongside it, never as brief_etag and never diffed; change detection is stated as unavailable until the etag lands, with refresh: true named as the only mitigation and the gap required in unverified.

Greptile P1 4141919348 was a real defect and is fixed. Two recorded commands held prose inside python3 -c and could not be re-run, while carrying exit_code 0 and being cited as evidence. Both now cite skills/desk-bootstrap/desk-production-loop/verify.sh, a committed script that runs from the checkout and is location-independent.

G-1 and G-3 pass for bot-00-programming-lead across all fifteen paths including the new verify.sh. No .py file was added, because **/*.py resolves to bot-01-systems-backend.

unverified: The live memory_brief response was never observed in this session — the substrate/Hermes connector is not reachable from this cloud container, so whether substrate memory_brief returns an etag at all is unverified. What IS verified from the code is that the gateway's desk_brief does not (services/desk-gateway core.brief returns seat, generated_at, substrate, recall, loaded_packs, intake_queue, reminders, cached). The skill therefore requires a recorded revision marker rather than an etag specifically: the etag where a tool's contract has one, and desk_brief.generated_at otherwise. A successful brief from an etag-less tool is explicitly NOT degraded — Greptile P1 4141824942 caught the earlier wording, which would have degraded every gateway turn on the desk.

No memory_brief, memory_write, events_emit, graph_get or handoff_to_hermes call was made. The tool names, kinds and failure semantics are transcribed from contracts/tool-rosters/_core.yaml, docs/upgrade-plan-desk-v2.md §4 and docs/vps-agent-bus.md §2, not from a live call.

brief_etag on this receipt is null because this run could not brief at all: no connector, so desk_brief/memory_brief was never listed. Under the corrected §3 that is genuinely degraded (tool not listed), not the etag-less-tool case — a LEAD docs turn in a container with no connector is the skill's own first example.

The etag is not threaded through the roster schemas. contracts/tool-rosters/_core.yaml gives desk_brief no etag output and desk_memory_retain / desk_event_emit no etag input, and every roster schema is additionalProperties: false, so passing one today would be a validation error. The receipt is the only place it is recorded until QUALITY lands that contract change (G-4). The skill says so explicitly rather than implying the field already flows.

The five packet_* field names for the signed handoff are provisional placeholders for SPE-4792, which has not landed. They are documented as omit-do-not-send, and no signature, digest or key id was computed or invented. When SPE-4792 ships, its schema wins and the table in the skill §7 and docs/vps-agent-bus.md is the thing to correct.

skills.approve does not exist as a capability anywhere in this repository. The rule is written as a standing restriction (list and invoke only) plus the condition that would lift it; it is not a claim that such a capability is being built or scheduled.

No new event kind was minted, so nothing here was verified against a live consumer. Degradation is signalled in payload.degraded on the kind that matches the outcome — implementation.completed for a finished degraded turn, ticket.blocked only for a turn that stopped without an ack. docs/handoff-contracts.md is QUALITY's contract surface and a dedicated loop.* kind is a G-4 change LEAD cannot make.

The root .mcp.json still configures the hindsight and ragflow HTTP MCP servers. That file is bot-05-infrastructure's, so this change documents the boundary (Lane A cloud-session tooling, never a desk seat default) instead of editing it. Actually removing or re-scoping those entries is an INFRA ticket and is NOT done by this PR.

skills/README.md still has no row for desk-production-loop. That file is bot-06-quality-security's; adding the row here would be the same cross-seat edit that PR #4's receipt already recorded as a deliberate G-1 violation. QUALITY adds the row.

The CI Quality Gates workflow will not attribute this branch. .github/workflows/gates.yml derives the acting bot from the branch prefix and requires ^bot-0[0-6]-[a-z0-9-]+$; this branch is claude/spe-4794-production-loop-v4i18e, so the 'Determine the acting bot' step exits 1 before G-1 runs. The gates recorded above were therefore run locally with --bot bot-00-programming-lead. A re-push under bot-00-programming-lead/spe-4794-production-loop would let CI run them, and needs the dispatcher's go-ahead since the branch name was pinned by the work order.
Greptile was not run — that is QUALITY's gate, not LEAD's.
ci/gates/run_all.py was not invoked as a suite; the individual gates relevant to this diff (G-1 manifest, G-1 per-branch, G-3, G-7, G-2) are recorded above.

The Greptile fixes are documentation-level and were verified by content assertions plus the repo's own gates, not by running a seat through the loop against a live gateway. Whether a seat actually follows the corrected §3 and §6 is observable only once the loop runs on a real ticket.

Whether the substrate memory_brief reached through the Hermes connector nests its upstream failure the same way desk_brief does is unverified — the connector was not reachable. The skill therefore states the rule concretely for desk_brief (substrate.error / recall.error, verified from the gateway source) and, for memory_brief, tells the seat to find the field that says the upstream failed rather than accept the envelope. That instruction is a discipline, not a transcribed field name.

verify.sh asserts that the rules are PRESENT in the prose and that superseded wording is gone. It cannot assert that the rules are correct, or that a seat follows them. Two review rounds have now corrected rules that the earlier version of this check would have passed, which is the honest measure of its limits.
blockers: SPE-4792 (signed handoff packet schema) has not landed, so handoff_to_hermes stays unsigned and the packet fields stay omitted. Documented, not worked around.

A top-level skills/desk-production-loop/ directory needs one last-match rule in ownership.yaml from QUALITY. Until then the skill lives under skills/desk-bootstrap/desk-production-loop/, and skills/README.md's map row is also QUALITY's to add.
Threading the brief etag through desk_brief, desk_memory_retain and desk_event_emit is a contracts/tool-rosters/** change, which is QUALITY's contract surface (G-4).

desk_doctor does not require desk-production-loop. _declared_skills() in services/desk-gateway/src/desk_gateway/tools/core.py derives the required list from prompts/<bot_id>.xml plus a hard-coded ('verification-receipts', 'desk-doctor', 'desk-bootstrap'), so a seat can omit the new mandatory default and still get a green skills row. Proposed patch: add 'desk-production-loop' to that tuple. That file is bot-01-systems-backend's, so it is a SYSTEMS one-liner; alternatively each seat adds <skill path="skills/desk-bootstrap/desk-production-loop/SKILL.md" load="always"/> to its own prompt source, which would also need QUALITY to regenerate prompts-assembled/. LEAD did neither rather than edit foreign paths (G-1). Raised by Greptile P2 4141824957.
